description: The plot illustrates the training loss over time for two models: “Vanilla” and “SepLLM,” as described in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis represents “Training Time (s)” on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 250,000 seconds, with major tick marks at intervals of 50,000 seconds. The y-axis shows “Loss,” also on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, with tick marks at 0.05 intervals. The “Vanilla” model is represented by a purple line with triangular markers, starting at approximately 2.75 loss at 0 seconds and gradually decreasing to about 2.50 by 250,000 seconds. The “SepLLM” model is shown with a red line and circular markers, beginning at roughly 2.72 loss and declining more steeply to approximately 2.49 by 250,000 seconds. A green dashed horizontal line at loss = 2.50 and vertical lines at ~200,000 and ~250,000 seconds highlight a performance comparison, with a label “1.26×” indicating that SepLLM reaches the target loss 1.26 times faster than Vanilla. Both lines exhibit a smooth, monotonic decline, with SepLLM consistently achieving lower loss at equivalent training times.
